page.layout: One page of text, one column; running head above the text; page number top right; below the text an acrostic list of lines with letters in the left margin; catchword at the foot right; signature "d 3" centred at the foot. Left margin holds marginal letters/signs of the acrostic.

main_text.p: codex canonum vocatur, Carolo Magno oblatam esse. Hoc declarant plurima, quæ in Bibliothecis Galliæ visuntur, Collectionis hujus exemplaria: quorum in fronte, velut oblati muneris dedicatio præfixa est, Hadriani ad Carolum epistola, quæ primis singulorum versuum litteris hunc titulum reddit, Domino Excell. Filio Carulo Regi Hadrianus Papa. Epistola autem ipsa sic habet, tum in aliis passim, tum in vetustissimo S. Germani codice, Caroli ipsius Magni temporibus exarato, anno regni ejus xxxvii. id est Christi DCCCV.
main_text.head: EPISTOLA HADRIANI PAPÆ AD CAROLUM MAGNUM REGEM,
Quæ in antiquis exemplaribus Codici Canonum præponitur.
main_text.p: DIVINA fulgens doctrina sceptra præcellit regni,
main_text.l: Origo regum felix, semper genitura beata,
Molem perspicimus legis gratiam laudis habere.
Iusto gignitur rege Ecclesiæ almæ defensor,
Numquam enim vinci potest disciplina cælestis,
Olim jam fumens paterni triumphans regni
Exemplum, quo devota fides victoria gaudet,
Christo juvante, ac beato clavigero Petro,
Cunctas adversas gentes regalibus subdit plantis.
En radix beata instar contulit prole.
Læta Deum colere, legem semper amare divinam,
Laudabilem servare fidem, sanctamque defendere vitam,
Fautorem prorsus habens janitorem in triumphis cæli.
Ipsius freta virtute victrice persistit semper.

page.notes: Left margin carries acrostic letters (D, O, M, I, N, O, E, C, C, E, L, L, F, I) printed beside the verse lines, partly illegible in the scan. Initial D is a large woodcut-style letter. Verse lines are short and the first line is set with a large initial; the Gothic-like "Iusto" and "Ecclesiæ" are as printed.
